nodes.summary: For `1 ≤ k`, a real `x` lies below the `k`-th smallest value of `f` iff fewer than `k` values of `f` are strictly below `x`.
nodes.title: Strict-count criterion for the order statistic

nodes.summary: For `α < 1` and `k = ⌈(1 - α)(n + 1)⌉`, the test score is covered by the threshold `q̂` (the `k`-th smallest calibration score, or `⊤` if `k > n`) iff the coordinate-permutation p-value of the test coordinate exceeds `α`. Ties are allowed.
nodes.title: Split conformal coverage as a permutation test

nodes.summary: For `1 ≤ k`, the test score is covered by the threshold iff fewer than `k` calibration scores lie strictly below it, i.e. `L ≤ k - 1`.
nodes.title: Coverage through the strict lower count

nodes.summary: The coordinate-permutation action moves the entry at `σ⁻¹ i` to position `i`.
nodes.title: Entries of a permuted vector

nodes.summary: If the law `μ` of the score vector is a probability measure invariant under every coordinate permutation, then with `k = ⌈(1 - α)(n + 1)⌉` the test score is covered by the `k`-th smallest calibration score (`⊤` if `k > n`) with probability at least `k / (n + 1)` (Vovk, Gammerman and Shafer 2005; Lei et al. 2018). The proof applies validity of the permutation p-value at the grid level `(n + 1 - k) / (n + 1)`. The…
nodes.title: Split conformal coverage at the grid level

nodes.summary: If the law of the score vector is a probability measure invariant under every coordinate permutation, the test score is covered by the split conformal threshold with probability at least `1 - α`. The recorded scope is `0 < α < 1`; the statement assumes only `0 ≤ α < 1`, and the endpoint `α = 0` (coverage `1`) is a derived trivial case, not attributed to the sources.
nodes.title: Split conformal coverage

nodes.summary: For `1 ≤ k`, the `k`-th smallest value of `f` is `x` iff fewer than `k` values are strictly below `x` and at least `k` values are at most `x`: the usual characterisation of the `k`-th order statistic with multiplicity.
nodes.title: Characterisation of the order statistic

nodes.summary: For `1 ≤ k`, the `k`-th smallest value of `f` is `⊤` exactly when `f` has fewer than `k` values.
nodes.title: The order statistic is infinite exactly past the sample size

nodes.summary: The `k`-th smallest value of `f`, counted with multiplicity: the least value `f i` such that at least `k` indices `j` satisfy `f j ≤ f i`. It is `⊤` when no value qualifies, which for `1 ≤ k` happens exactly when `k > Fintype.card ι` (`orderStatistic_eq_top_iff`). For `k = 0` it is the minimum of `f` (a junk value; the results below assume `1 ≤ k`).
nodes.title: Order statistic with multiplicity

nodes.summary: With the coordinate-permutation action `(σ • ω) i = ω (σ⁻¹ i)` and the statistic `ω ↦ ω (Fin.last n)`, the permutation p-value is `(n + 1 - L) / (n + 1)`, where `L` is the number of calibration scores strictly below the test score. Each coordinate is moved to the test position by `n!` permutations.
nodes.title: Permutation p-value of the test score

nodes.summary: A law on `ι → β` that is invariant under every coordinate permutation `ω ↦ ω ∘ σ` is invariant under the coordinate-permutation action.
nodes.title: Permutation-invariant laws are invariant under the action

nodes.summary: The `k`-th smallest calibration score `ω i.castSucc` (with multiplicity), and `⊤` when `k > n`.
nodes.title: Split conformal threshold

nodes.summary: The strict lower count is below `⌈(1 - α)(n + 1)⌉` iff `α` is below the coordinate-permutation p-value `(n + 1 - L) / (n + 1)`. No restriction on `α` is needed.
nodes.title: Rank threshold versus p-value threshold

nodes.summary: The number of calibration scores `ω i.castSucc` strictly below the test score `ω (Fin.last n)`.
nodes.title: Strict lower count of the test score
